teaching.causalExplanation: Two words sit at the centre of this, and they're easy to mix up. Equality means everyone gets the same. Equity means everyone gets what they need to reach a similar outcome. Suppose a state gives every school the same ten thousand dollars for a health program. That's equality. A school where students already eat well and see a doctor turns it into a small gain. But a school where a third of students skip meals, and the nearest clinic is an hour away, needs different things first. Same money, different starting points, and the gap gets wider. One careful point. Not every difference in health is unfair. Older people have more chronic disease than younger people, and nobody could remove that difference completely. A difference counts as an inequity only when it passes three tests. It's avoidable, it's unnecessary, and it's unfair. Showing that a gap passes those three tests is part of your argument. Don't just assume it. Now access. A service that exists isn't the same as a service you can use. There are at least six kinds of barrier. Financial, which isn't just the fee, it's lost wages, petrol and childcare too. Geographic, the distance, and whether a bus runs when the service is open. Cultural, whether the service feels safe and respectful to your community. Language and literacy. Physical, whether the building works for people with disability. And informational, whether people even know it exists.

scenes.teachingReason: Two words sit at the centre of this, and they're easy to mix up. Equality means everyone gets the same. Equity means everyone gets what they need to reach a similar outcome. Suppose a state gives every school the same ten thousand dollars for a health program. That's equality. A school where students already eat well and see a doctor turns it into a small gain. But a school where a third of students skip meals, and the nearest clinic is an hour away, needs different things first. Same money, different starting points, and the gap gets wider.

Asking for comments on a plan that's already finished is consultation, not participation.

scenes.teachingReason: A right is an entitlement you hold because you're a person. The same World Health Organization constitution you met earlier says the highest attainable standard of health is a fundamental right of every human being. So care can't depend on whether someone seems to deserve it, like a smoker with lung disease, or a driver hurt while speeding. Two limits keep this honest. A right doesn't mean unlimited resources. And a right on paper, with no access, isn't yet a right in practice.

scenes.teachingReason: So how do these principles actually improve health status? Here's the mechanism. The group furthest behind carries the most ill health that could be avoided. When help is matched to what that group needs, the same effort removes far more ill health there than in a group that's already close to the best it can be. So equity isn't just fair. It's often one of the most effective ways to lift a whole population. And the four work as a chain. A right nobody can reach changes nothing, and a service nobody trusts doesn't get used.

scenes.teachingReason: It's access, through a language and literacy barrier. The materials exist, but a quarter of the district can't use them. A good change is translating them into the main community languages, or providing interpreters at education sessions, ideally designed with those communities. The classic mistake is calling it equality, just because everyone gets the same leaflet.

scenes.motionPurpose:
Heading on screen: "Key notes: what to write in your book".

1. Equality: everyone gets the same. Equity: what each needs for a similar outcome.
2. Inequity: a difference that is avoidable, unnecessary and unfair.
3. Access barriers: financial, geographic, cultural, language, physical, informational.
4. Participation: people affected help design, run and judge it (not just consulted).
5. Rights: entitlement to the highest attainable standard of health; no "deserve".

Memory card (the scene 9 card) beside the notes. Notes 38 px in the principle colours; each bullet one line of at most 86 characters. Hold about 45 seconds in all.
